summary.text: 前 commonly means ‘in front’ or ‘before.’ Its graphic history is disputed: one account links it to 歬, while another says a cutting graph was reused for the directional word. The sources do not resolve which graph came first.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. A traditional analysis explains 歬 as 止 above 舟, interpreted as a boat moving forward. Competing accounts associate 前 with a cutting graph and propose that it was later used for the directional word; the available evidence does not establish the graph sequence.

components.text: In the related graph 歬, 止 is placed above 舟. The reported analysis interprets their combination as a boat moving forward; this is an account of 歬, not proof of 前’s origin.
In 歬, 舟 represents the boat in the reported picture of forward movement. This component analysis belongs to 歬, not to the current graph 前.

history.text: 前 is listed among bronze forms, including forms indexed to Western Zhou material, and is also recorded in small-seal script. These records do not establish the earliest lexical meaning; no character-specific glyph image is supplied here.

The accounts conflict over the graph history: one treats 歬 as the directional graph and 前 as a later way of writing its word; another associates 前 with cutting and treats 歬 as the older directional form. The sources do not settle the sequence.

In the cutting account, 前 was reused to write the directional word associated with 歬. This is a proposed borrowing between words, not a demonstrated change in meaning. The proposal depends on a supposed sound resemblance, but no independent name and pronunciation for a depicted tool are established; 前’s reconstructed reading alone cannot prove the match.
A separate account analyzes 剪 as 刀 plus 歬 serving as a sound element. Sources also report cutting-related uses written with 前, but they do not establish a sequence leading to the modern forms.

uncertainties.text: The accounts disagree over whether 歬 or a cutting graph involving 刀 came first in the history of directional 前; the sequence remains unresolved.
The available citations do not securely date the earliest lexical use or establish the order of motion, spatial, and temporal uses. Dictionary glosses alone do not determine that chronology.
The proposed cutting-related borrowing lacks an independently established name and pronunciation for the depicted implement, so the proposed sound match is unverified.
Written descriptions support discussion of the reported forms and analyses, but no usable character-specific glyph image is included.

senses.text: 前 is used for a position in front and for forward direction. The evidence does not securely date the historical emergence of these uses.
前 also means earlier in time or preceding. Its historical development in relation to the spatial sense is not established.

developments.text: Spatial and temporal uses are documented, but their relationship and chronology are not established.

limitations.text: Bronze and seal-form records do not date the first lexical use or establish an earliest meaning for 前. Forward motion is a reported interpretation of 歬, not a proven original sense of 前.
The cutting use may concern a distinct word written with the same graph. The proposed sound-based borrowing is not demonstrated by an independently attested object-name comparison.

overview.text: 前 means ‘in front’ or ‘before.’ One account links it to 歬, pictured as a boat moving forward. Another proposes that a cutting graph was reused for direction based on a supposed sound resemblance; the implement’s original name and pronunciation are not independently established.

relationships.text: A dictionary identifies 歬 as a variant of 前. This records a graphic relationship without deciding which form is historically earlier.
